plan: Hold the workspace as a single deep-copied dictionary tree so the constructor argument and to_data() output are isolated from internal state.
Provide one recursive generator (_walk) yielding (item, depth) in document order; build total_word_count, unresolved_markers, and outline on top of it so all traversals agree.
Count note words by first replacing every [[?identifier]] marker with a space, then counting \b\w+\b matches; add each reference's declared word_count.
Collect unresolved identifiers from note-text markers and reference 'unresolved' lists into a set, returned sorted lexicographically.
Render the outline as the workspace title followed by one line per item: two spaces per nesting level plus '<kind>: <title>'.

Implement move with full validation before any mutation: string-typed ids, item existence, literal 'workspace' or a section/group destination, rejection of self/descendant destinations via a subtree scan, and integer index within 0..len(destination); only then pop from the source list and append or insert.
Return a deep copy from to_data() so failed moves are trivially non-mutating and callers cannot alias internal state.
mechanisms: marker-stripping regex preprocessing before word tokenization
validate-then-mutate move with subtree containment (cycle) check
deep-copy export for immutability of failed operations
